title: Memory Rooms scene v1 + v2
description: The layout contract for one memory spot. Units are metres; the floor is y = 0; x runs west -> east, z runs north -> south. Interior origin = the room's north-west floor corner (v2 polygon: the outline's bounding box starts at [0, 0]; v2 room in a building: the north-west corner of the room's wall-centreline bounding box, on its level's floor); exterior origin = the centre of the site. `at` is the centre of an object's footprint on its base. rotY is degrees about +y (0 = the object's front faces south/+z, 90 = east, 180 = north, 270 = west). v1 = a box shell; v2 adds polygon shells (`shell.outline`), sloped ceilings (`shell.ceiling.shape`) and rooms inside a building (`shell: { building, room }`), CONTRACTS.md section 6. Validated by src/memory-rooms/scene/validate.js (JS) and tools/memory-rooms/blender/scene_io.py (Python), which implement the same keyword subset.

version.description: 1 = box shell only. 2 = also polygon shells, sloped ceilings and rooms inside a building.

notes.description: Free text for the modeller (Claude). Not shown on the site.

hero.description: Optional override for the 3/4 hero shot used on the map card. Omit to let Blender frame it.

size3.description: [w, h, d] in metres: w along the object's local x (side to side), h up, d along its local z (back to front).

kit.description: Interior pieces, exterior pieces, then glb (imported asset) and bespoke (a Blender function in memory-rooms-work/<spot>/bespoke/<script>.py). An unknown name fails validation.

material.description: Names in tools/memory-rooms/blender/materials.py. Each is procedural and tinted by the object's color (or accent).

shell.description: The room. Three shapes: a box (width, depth, height; v1 and v2), a polygon (v2: outline + height) or a room of a building (v2: building + room; everything else comes from building.json).

width.description: Box: interior size along x (west -> east wall).

depth.description: Box: interior size along z (north -> south wall).

height.description: Floor to ceiling (a sloped ceiling: the walls at the eaves).

outline.description: v2 polygon room: the inner faces of the walls, [x, z] corners in order (either direction). Its bounding box starts at [0, 0]. Edge i runs from outline[i] to outline[i + 1] (the last one back to the first); openings name it with `edge`, and its GLB wall is `wall__e<i>`.

building.description: v2 room inside a building: the building id (memory_buildings.id). Walls, floor, ceiling and openings come from its building.json.

room.description: v2 room inside a building: the room id in building.json.

thickness.description: Built OUTSIDE the interior box, so width/depth stay exact. Default 0.12.

skirting.description: Skirting boards along the floor. Default true.

ceiling.description: Flat by default. v2 sloped ceilings: the shell `height` is the walls at the eaves and `peak` the highest point. gable: a ridge running along `axis` at `ridgeAt` (measured across the other axis; default the middle of the bounding box); the walls under the ridge's ends rise to it; `eaves` = [low side, high side] heights when they differ. pyramid: every wall at the eaves, rising to `peak` at `apex` (default the outline's centroid). skillion: one plane, `height` on the `low` side and `peak` on the opposite side.

show.description: Default true. The viewer hides it in dollhouse view either way.

peak.description: v2: ridge (gable), apex (pyramid) or high side (skillion) height.

axis.description: v2 gable: the direction the ridge runs (x = west-east, z = north-south). Default: along the longer side of the bounding box.

ridgeAt.description: v2 gable: where the ridge sits across the other axis (axis x: a z value; axis z: an x value). Default: the middle.

eaves.description: v2 gable: [eave height on the low-coordinate side, on the high-coordinate side] when the two differ. Default: both = the shell height.

apex.description: v2 pyramid: [x, z] of the apex. Default: the outline's centroid.

low.description: v2 skillion: the side the ceiling falls to.

shellV1Rules.description: What a version 1 scene may not use (the v2 additions).

opening.description: A door, window or open gap in one wall. Box shells name the wall (`wall`); v2 polygon shells name the edge (`edge`). offset runs along the wall from its lower-x end (north/south walls) or lower-z end (east/west walls), or along an edge from outline[edge] toward the next corner, to the opening's near edge.

edge.description: v2 polygon shells: the outline edge (0 = outline[0] -> outline[1]).

sill.description: Height of the bottom edge above the floor. Doors and openings: 0 (the default). Windows: default 0.9.

open.description: Doors: how far the leaf swings open (0 shut, 1 = 90 degrees). Default 0.

size.description: [w, d] of the ground plate, centred on the origin.

terrain.description: A real-world landscape diorama built from elevation data (tools/memory-rooms/landscape/): [w, d] centred on the origin, heights [base, top] in metres. The viewer frames this box, sets the drafting table under the base and offers no walk-in or AR.

vexag.description: Vertical exaggeration baked into the GLB (1 = true scale).

at.description: Centre of the footprint, on the object's base (y = base height).

mount.description: How it is held up. Omit to let check-scene infer it (floor if y = 0, on if it rests on another object's top, wall/ceiling if it touches one). 'free' opts out of the float check.

overlaps.description: Ids this object may interpenetrate on purpose (a chair tucked under a desk, a rug under a bed).

footprint.description: Optional plan outline, [x, z] corners in the scene frame, for a piece that is not a box in plan (a loft or bench fitted to an angled wall). check-scene tests the walls and the ceiling at these corners instead of the box's; it must lie inside the box's footprint, and only bespoke or glb pieces may have one (a kit draws its box). Blender ignores it.

script.description: bespoke only: memory-rooms-work/<spot>/bespoke/<script>.py, which defines build(ctx, spec).

src.description: glb only: path relative to the spot's work folder.

params.description: Kit-specific options (see tools/memory-rooms/blender/kit/README.md). Unknown keys are ignored by the kit.

photos.description: Which photos show it (documentation for the compare loop).

type.description: lamp/pendant: warm point light at `at`. ceiling: area light just under the ceiling. spot/area: aimed at `look`. window: daylight through every window (no `at`). sun: the sun (interior through openings; exterior with the sky).

intensity.description: Relative: 1 = a normal light of its type.

size.description: Radius (lamp) or side length (area/ceiling) in metres.

from.description: sun only: compass direction the sun shines FROM.

azimuth.description: sun only: degrees clockwise from north, overrides `from`.

elevation.description: sun only: degrees above the horizon.

object.description: Id of the object this light belongs to (a lamp's shade glows).

camera.description: Where photo N was taken from. fov = field of view across the photo's LONG edge in degrees (phone main camera ~ 68-73; 0.5x ultrawide ~ 105-120). aspect = photo width / height (0.75 portrait, 1.333 landscape). photo: 1-12 for the shot guide, up to 40 for a freeform spot (old photos, CONTRACTS.md 8). fit: how well the render could place it (old photos: 'rough' cameras are drawn fainter, 'roughly here'); absent = good.

roll.description: Degrees, positive = clockwise as seen by the photographer.

fit.description: How well the render placed this photo (a freeform spot: every used photo is a camera so the viewer can fly to it). rough = drawn fainter in the viewer, 'roughly here'. Absent = good.

frame.description: Places this room in a shared building frame: the room's origin sits at `origin` = [x, z] in the group frame, rotated by rotY about +y, lifted by y (upper floors). The v1 way to assemble a house (still valid in v2); a v2 room inside a building uses shell.building instead and has no frame.
